title: Datastores
description: Backing stores for the application. Postgres is the system of record; blob holds the data room.

rls.description: What the application ASKS for. fail_closed = a query with no workspace in scope returns zero rows; on = policies are enforced but permissive when no workspace is set; off = no tenant isolation. fail_closed and on are GATES: provision.py refuses to finish a deploy that cannot prove them, and factory.py validate refuses either value on a stamped app without a matching rls_verified block.

rls_verified.description: EVIDENCE, written by provision.py/clone.py from a live measurement of the database the app runs against — never by hand. This is what turns `rls` from a claim into a record: it names the role that was measured, how many org-scoped tables were enabled+forced+policied, and whether another workspace's rows were actually readable.

at.description: The instant of the measurement, as an RFC 3339 date-time WITH offset (provision.py's NOW, e.g. 2026-09-09T14:03:27+00:00). factory.py validate orders this exactly against infrastructure.deployed_at and refuses an offset-less value; the schema pattern now refuses the same spellings, so schema and reader agree for every timestamp they share, not only deployed_at (mold_v1-053).

backend.description: Which Postgres backend was measured (the datastores.postgres.provider value), so a proof against the local self_hosted database is never mistaken for a proof against the managed one

source.description: Which command produced this, or why nothing could be proven

role.description: current_user on the deployed DATABASE_URL — app_rw, not postgres

bypassrls.description: Must be false: BYPASSRLS silently ignores every policy, and FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY does not override it

org_scoped_tables.description: Tables in public carrying an org_id column, counted from the catalog

protected.description: Of those, how many have RLS enabled AND forced AND at least one policy

open_policies.description: Permissive policies that apply to the app role and do NOT scope by org_id. Postgres OR's permissive policies, so each one reopens its whole table. Must be empty

leaking_policies.description: Permissive policies that were EXECUTED as the app role against rows the check owns and handed over another workspace's rows anyway — a predicate can name org_id and still say `OR true`. Must be empty

policies_executed.description: How many permissive policies were run, one at a time, on a temp copy of their table's columns. This is the measurement that reaches the tables the live probe skips for their foreign keys or triggers

policies_unverified.description: Policies that could not be executed (the app role lacks TEMP, the admin cannot SET ROLE to it, the table's shape could not be replicated). An unverified policy is never counted as a passing one

unmeasured.description: Org-scoped tables that neither the cross-workspace probe nor the policy execution pass could measure — nothing proves those tables. Must be empty

probe_table.description: The table the cross-workspace read/write probe ran against, inside a rolled-back transaction

probe_tables.description: How many tables the cross-workspace read/write probe actually ran on (it runs on every eligible table, not one)

probe_skipped.description: Tables the live probe could not use, each with the reason (foreign keys, user triggers, control plane, unsynthesisable column) — so a probe count is never read as 'all of them'

foreign_rows_readable.description: Rows of another workspace visible to the app role while scoped. Must be 0

leaking_tables.description: Tables that returned another workspace's rows, with counts. Must be empty

cross_org_write.description: SQLSTATE of the cross-workspace INSERT. Must be 42501; 'ACCEPTED' means the write went through

cross_org_writable.description: Tables that accepted a row owned by another workspace, with the SQLSTATE returned. Must be empty

unset_org_rows.description: fail_closed only: rows visible with app.org_id set to the empty string, which is what a transaction pooler leaves behind. Must be 0

open_with_no_org.description: fail_closed only: tables that still returned rows with app.org_id set to the empty string. Must be empty

running_app.description: VERDICT on what the app IN FRONT OF TRAFFIC says on /api/ops/health, as one of exactly three tokens. The stored credential passing the gate is a different fact from the running build using it (a Vercel env change only takes effect on the next build), so this is the only reading that covers the serving process. CONTRACT (provision.py writes, factory.py reads, nothing else parses this): `enforced` = the health body carried this mold's own affirmative sentence `role <name> (RLS enforced)` for the role the serving process connects as, i.e. pg_roles.rolbypassrls was measured false; the only value that lets a stamped app validate. `not_enforced` = the health body reported BYPASSRLS or `row-level security is NOT enforced`: a definitive reading that the running build holds the wrong DATABASE_URL, and only a new build (--deploy) clears it. `unmeasured` = nothing usable was read: no production URL, an unreachable or non-2xx endpoint, a login wall, a body without a db check, a db check that is not the affirmative sentence, or the app could not reach its database. Unmeasured is never good news; it fails validate like not_enforced does. The human-readable sentence (HTTP status, the db.detail text, the reason nothing could be read) goes in running_app_detail, NEVER here: factory.py compares this field for equality against the three tokens and reads nothing else, so any other spelling ("Enforced", "enforced — ...", "NOT enforced") is a schema error, not a verdict.

running_app_detail.description: Free text beside running_app for the operator: the db.detail sentence the health endpoint returned, or why it could not be read (`HTTP 404 DEPLOYMENT_NOT_FOUND`, `no production URL yet`). Printed, never parsed — no reader may derive a verdict from it. Write it together with running_app on every outcome.

scope.description: fresh = own database; shared_with_live = the live source deployment's database, crons stripped on deploy

source.description: live_source_agent = a snapshot of the live source deployment

taken_at.description: When the snapshot was taken, as an RFC 3339 date-time WITH offset (clone.py's NOW). Ordered exactly against rls_verified.at by factory.py validate and clone.py, which refuse an offset-less value; the pattern refuses it at the schema too (mold_v1-053).

snapshot.description: Where the initial data came from when cloning

sslmode.description: The runtime clients pass NO ssl option (agent/lib/db/index.ts, lib/ops-db.ts), so this query parameter on DATABASE_URL is the only thing that turns TLS on. Without it the app speaks plaintext Postgres.

admin_url_ref.description: Secret NAME of the URL with DDL rights (migrations, pg_restore). Never DATABASE_URL after the app_rw bootstrap: that role owns nothing.

pooling.description: transaction = DATABASE_URL is a transaction pooler (Neon pooled endpoint, Supabase Supavisor:6543). Safe for RLS: app.org_id is set with set_config(...,true), which is transaction-local.

exposure.description: How the database is reachable. There is no public-port option, by design. remote_loopback (target vm_remote): the app's own cluster on the deployed server, listening on 127.0.0.1 only, behind a firewall that opens 22/80/443 and nothing else.

provider.description: fs (target vm_remote only): files on the deployed server's disk under infrastructure.vm_remote.storage.dir.

source.description: live_source_agent = a snapshot of the live source deployment

taken_at.description: When the snapshot was taken, as an RFC 3339 date-time WITH offset (clone.py's NOW). Ordered exactly against rls_verified.at by factory.py validate and clone.py, which refuse an offset-less value; the pattern refuses it at the schema too (mold_v1-053).
